title: apply and map, and why they are the slow path

videos.script: Here is a function that takes one trip and returns how long it took. {{function}} apply calls it on every row of the table. It reads well, and the answer is right. {{apply}} It is also about five hundred times slower than one line on two columns. {{slower}} apply is a loop in disguise. Every call builds a row and runs Python, thirty-three thousand times. {{loop}} This lesson takes the usual reasons for reaching for it, one at a time. {{reasons}} A lookup is a map with a dictionary. A chain of ifs is np.select. A group statistic is a name pandas already knows. {{replacements}} And it keeps apply for what it is good at. Logic that needs Python, run on few enough pieces that the loop does not matter. {{keep}} Twelve months is few. Thirty thousand rows is not. Measure before you decide. {{end}}
